_doc: Journeys J1-J7 of KIN-CONTINUE-003 as route-level walks of the REAL console (rsi/runtime/ux/walk.mjs). `steps` are declarative: goto <path> | click <text-regex or css> | gone <css> | focus <css> | fill <css> <text> | hover <text-regex or css> | key <chord> | place <picker-css> | enabled <text-regex or css> | send <text-regex or css> | wait text=<literal> | wait css=<selector> | url <regex> | value <css> <string> | shot <name>. Selectors are best-effort (zh+en); a selector prefixed with `?` is optional (empty-daemon / missing seed) and is recorded as skipped; any other missing or failed action is a hard failure. `focus` exists for a trigger inside a composer: the field blurs, the page re-lays-out, and a mouse click lands on the wrapper; focus then `key Enter` is the accessible path and the stable one. `place` opens the working-directory picker, chooses a listed place or a project root the daemon reports, and records `<journey>-<vp>-skipped-no-workdir` (a skip, not a failure) when there is genuinely nothing to choose. `gone <css>` waits (RSI_UX_WAIT_MS, default 15000) until no visible match of the selector remains and is a hard failure when one is still on screen at the deadline; it proves a decision landed and took its control off the screen. `enabled` asserts a control is usable without pressing it (a throwaway daemon has no fake agent, so starting a run would launch a real CLI); a disabled control is a hard failure unless the page names the missing prerequisite on screen. `send` is the press itself: it keeps that disabled verdict, then asks the daemon's /api/agents whether the claude-code binary lives under a directory named journeys_fake_agent (the seed's own test), records `<journey>-<vp>-skipped-no-fake-agent` with the reason and never clicks when it does not, and only then clicks and waits for /tasks/<id>. A walk must never launch a real CLI. `wait` waits until that literal text / selector is VISIBLE (timeout RSI_UX_WAIT_MS, default 15000; a timeout is a hard failure). `url` waits until the current pathname matches the regex. `value` asserts an input's current value. `paths` maps changed files to the journeys they can affect (first match wins; no match = all journeys). `viewports` are WxH. J7 reopens the seeded conversation after Back by pointer tap (`click [data-session-row="{conversation}"]`), so a surface covering the row reddens the walk; the keyboard path would hide that dead zone.
